title: Node Express Rules
summary: Project rules for Express services: routes, services and data layers, schema validation, central error middleware, structured logs and supertest.
description: Express does not impose structure, so a service often grows into route files that validate, query and format in one place. These rules separate those jobs and give errors a single exit.
They also cover the production basics an agent forgets: request validation, structured logging, graceful shutdown and tests that never open a real port.
useWhen: You are building or extending an Express API
Error responses come in several shapes
Server code and app setup are tangled together
body:
# Project rules: Express

## Structure
- Split `app.ts` (builds and exports the Express app) from `server.ts` (listens and handles shutdown). Tests import the app only.
- Layers per feature: `routes` map URLs, `controllers` handle req and res, `services` hold logic, `repositories` talk to the database. Lower layers never import `req` or `res`.

## Requests
- Validate `body`, `params` and `query` with Zod or similar in a middleware before the handler runs. Trust nothing past that point unvalidated.
- Add `helmet`, a body size limit and rate limiting on public routes. Configure CORS with an explicit origin list.

## Errors
- Throw typed errors (`NotFoundError`, `ValidationError`) carrying a status. Wrap async handlers, or use Express 5 which forwards rejections, so none escape.
- One error middleware, registered last, returns `{ error: { code, message } }`. It logs the stack and hides it from clients.

## Logging and config
- Use pino with a request id; never `console.log` in code that ships. Never log tokens or passwords.
- Parse environment variables once at startup into a typed config object and fail fast if one is missing.

## Runtime
- Handle SIGTERM: stop accepting connections, finish in-flight requests, close the database pool.

## Tests
- Vitest or Jest with supertest against the exported app. Mock only at the repository boundary.

## Before finishing
Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test`.

example.prompt: Add PATCH /users/:id to update a display name
example.result: The agent adds a Zod schema middleware, a service method that throws NotFoundError for missing users, and supertest cases for 200, 400 and 404.

faq.question: Does it assume TypeScript?
faq.answer: It is written with TypeScript in mind, but the layering and error rules apply to a JavaScript project as well.

faq.question: Why split app and server files?
faq.answer: Importing an app that has already started listening makes tests flaky. A separate server file keeps the port out of the test run.
